BASIC STITCHES
6.1
INTRODUCTION
1ust like it is necessary to first make a foundation before erecting a building, the basic
stitches form the foundation of sewing. These stitches can also be used to make the garment
more beautiful and attractive. It is essential for all beginners to know about the basic
stitches. Let us find out more in this lesson.
6.2
OBJECTIVE
After reading this lesson, you will be able to do the following:
•
use various kinds of stitches;
•
demonstrate the use ofthese stitches to teach others;
•
make your garments more beautiful and attractive by using these stitches.
6.3
MEANING OF STITCHES
The mark ofthread left on a piece of cloth when a threaded needle is moved in and out
ofthe cloth is known as a 'stitch'.
6.4
NEED FOR STITCHES
1.
Tojoin two pieces of cloth together
2.
For neatness and for finishing.

3.
To get a good shape.
4.
To control the cloth.

Permanent
Stitches
These stitches are left in the garment and are not removed after the garment is ready.
Hence they are known as permanent stitches. These are of the following types ;-
i)
Quilting
This stitch is used to sew together two or more than two layers of cloth. The needle is
inserted diagonally into the cloth and brought out in the other direction. Quilting is done
from the wrongside of the cloth, as a result of which only a very small stitch is seen on
the front and slightly larger zig-zag stitches are seen on the reverse. The stitch is used to
set the inner lapels in a coat. The stitch can be made either by hand or a special quilting
machine can be used for the purpose.
ii)
Back Stitch

iv)
Hemming
stitch
This stitch is used to fasten a raw edge which is to be turned in while hemming. The needle
is inserted into the single fabric first, two threads are taken up and then the needle enters
the very edge of the fold, where its drawn out. All the stitches are made parallel to each
other.

v)
. Buttonhole stitch
This stitch is used for making buttonholes, eyelets and other decoration on garments. To
make this stitch, the needles is inserted half a point behind the cut edge of the buttonhole
and the thread is looped over the needle. The stitch is worked all round the cut buttonhole
and the raw edges are thus secured. One end ofthe buttonhole is made straight.
Fig 6.5 Buttonhole stitch
vi)
Hook and eye
Hook and eye are used to close the open edges of a garment, e.g. in a blouse or in a pant.
But the hooks used in both cases are different. The hooks used in a blouse have two holes
and its eye is madeofthread.
The hook used in a pant has three holes and it has a metallic
eye. The hooks and the metallic eye are fixed with a chain stitch.
Fig·6.6 Eye

Temporary Stitches
These stitches are removed after the garment is ready. Hence they are known as temporary
stitches. These are of the following types:
i)
Basting stitch
This stitch isused while stitching any garment. This stitch is longer on the right side
and smaller on the wrong side. It is used to control silky and slippery fabrics.
Basting stitch is of two types:-
•
even basting stitch
•
uneven basting stitch

iv)
Thread Mark
This is also known as the 'loop stitch'. It is used to transfer the marking from one
layer of fabric to another. It is generally used on fabrics where the tracing wheel
or chalk can not be used for marking. It is most often used on woollen fabrics.
The stitch is made like the back stitch where the needle is inserted from behind
and then drawn up keeping the thread loose so that a loop is formed. This loop
is later cut in half so that the thread remains on both layers of fabric.

DECORATIVE
STITCHES
Various decorative stitches are used for decorating garments. Decorative stitches are as
follows:-
i)
Blanket stitch
This stitch is generally used to bind the edges of a blanket, hence the name 'blanket

ii)
Herring-bone
stitch
The herring-bone
stitch is worked from left to right in two lines alternatively. The
stitch on the bottom line lies between two stitches on the top line and vice-versa.
This is used to secure the edges in woolen fabrics which are too thick to be turned
in for hemming. The width of the stitch should not more than 2 threads. This is also
used
to decorate
children's

and decorate

Fish bone stitch
This stitch looks like the bones of a fish and is thus called the fish bone stitch. The
stitches are linked to each other. These stitches are used on thick fabrics and on
the gathers of children garments,
etc. The stitch is made by keeping the thread in
front ofthe
needle.

iv)
Feather Stitch
This stitch looks like the feathers of a bird. It is basically a loop stitch made by
taking diagonal stitches in the same direction. This is used to decorate bed sheets,
tablecloth and children's garments. Feather stitch can be made in two lines - called
single feather stitch or in three lines-called double feather stitch. It is made by
keeping the thread in front ofthe needle.
Fig 6.14 Fe~ther stitch
v)
Stem stitch
Thisstitch is also known as reverse back stitch. The stitch is taken from the wrong
side of the fabric. It gives the appearance of a stem which is why it is called the
stem stitch. It is used to embroider the stem of flowers etc. The stitch is made by
taking back stitches while keeping the thread towards oneself.
Fig 6.15 Stem Stitch
vi)
Chain Stitch
This stitch looks like a chain and is thus
calledachainstitch.Itismade by looping
the thread over the needle. The needle
is inserted in the same hole from which
it came out, thus making a chain of
loops.
Fig 6.16 Chain Stitch
vii)
Lazy Daisy Stitch
This is also made like the chain stitch. The difference is that individual loops are
tired down and no chain is made. This can be made in various colors and the stitch
is generally used to embroider flowers, etc.
